name: Richibucto
location: On the left bank of the Richibucto river, about eight miles front its mouth.
remarks: Transferred to the Dominion Government at Confederation. The reserve originally contained about 5,720 acres. Two-thirds of it was subdivided and a number of lots sold prior Confederation. (F 13,145.)

name: Buctouche
location: On the left bank of the Buctouche river, about three miles from its mouth.
remarks: Transferred to the Dominion Government at Confederation.

name: Indian Island reserve
location: A point on the mainland at the mouth of Gaspereau creek, opposite Richibucto island in Richibucto harbour.
remarks: A 'Special Reserve,' held by deed from J.C. Vanlour to the Roman Catholic Bishop of St. John for the use of the Indians. (File 132,215.)

name: Fort Folly
location: On the left bank of the Petitcodiac river, due west of the town of Dorchester.
remarks: Purchased by the Provincial Government and deeded to and held in trust by the Magistrates of the county of Westmoreland for the use of the Micmac Indians, Aug. 15, 1840. (File 61,717.)

name: The Brothers.
location: Two small islands near the south shore of Kennebecasis bay.
remarks: Transferred to the Dominion Government at Confederation.

name: Canons River.
location: In the parish of St. James, at the mouth of the Canons river, on the, left bank of the Cheputneticook river.
remarks: Transferred to the Dominion Government at Confederation.

name: Woodstock.
location: On the right bank of the River St. John, about two miles south of Woodstock.
remarks: Purchased May 22, 1851, by the Provincial Government, for the use of the Amalecite tribe of Indians at the Maductic. No. 281.

name: Oromocto.
location: In the parish of Burton, on the right bank of the River St. John.
remarks: Purchased by the Dominion Government, Sept. 12, 1895.

name: Restigouche.
location: At the mouth of the Restigouche river, adjacent to the west boundary of the township of Mann, county of Bonaventure.
remarks: This reserve is a portion of the area of land set apart and appropriated under the statute 14 and 15 Victoria, chapter 106, for the benefit of the Indian tribes in lower Canada. The total area of land set apart by the statute amounted to 230,000 acres.

name: Maria.
location: At the mouth of the Grand Cascapedia river, in the township of Maria, county of Bonaventure.
remarks: Settled on and claimed by the Indians from time immemorial.

name: Betsiamits.
location: At the mouth of the Betsiamits river, on the north shore of the St. Lawrence river, in the county of Saguenay.
tribe_band: Montagnais, Tadousacs, Papinachois, Nauthapis and other nomadic tribes.
remarks: A portion of the area set apart lander the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Ouiatchouan.
location: On the west shore of Lake St. John, in the county of Chicoutimi.
tribe_band: Montagnais of Lake St. John and Tadousac.
remarks: Originally consisted of the entire township, containing 23,000 acres, set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. The whole township, with the exception of the present reserve, has been surrendered, and is being sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Lorette.
location: In the county of Quebec, about eight miles from the city.
remarks: This village, which is said to have contained an area of 40 arpents, had been long occupied by the Hurons. They were confirmed in possession by a deed of gift from the Jesuit Fathers, dated February 26, 1794. The boundaries were defined by order of the courts in 1887.

name: Quarante Arpents.
location: In the county of Quebec, about three miles from Lorette.
remarks: Gift from the Jesuit Fathers, dated March 7, 1742, and again confirmed in the deed of gift of February 26, 1794, mentioned above.

name: Rocmont.
location: In the township of Rocmont, county of Portneuf.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Crespieul.
location: West of the township of Crespieul, in the county of Lake St. John.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Becancour.
location: Near Becancour, in the county of Nicolet. The reserve consists of lot No. 582 in the concession of the Indian Village, and Islands Nos. 574, 488 and 489 in the Becancour river.
remarks: These Indians were once the proprietors of the seigniory of Becancour, granted to them April 30, 1708. In 1760 they sold the of their territory, except the lot and islands which now constitute their reserve.

name: Pierreville
location: At Pierreville, in the county of Yamaska. Consists of the following lands Situated in the Seigniories of Pierreville and 9t. François du Lac, viz.:
remarks: Two large grants of land in Pierreville and St. Francis were made in 1700 and 1701 to these Indians by private parties. The present reserve is all they now possess, the whole of the remainder having been leased or otherwise conceded to whites.

name: 1217: Pierreville Reserve
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: 1218: 2nd con. St. Jacques or No. 1 on the especial plan
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: 1219: 3rd con. St. Jacques or No. 24 on the especial plan.
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: 880: a part of Ronde island
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: 850: a small island lying between Atcombac and Au Pin island
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: 874: parts of an island opposite Pierreville reserve
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).
Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: 482: 3rd con. parish of St. Francis. or No. 41 on the especial plan
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: 972: lot in the village of Pierreville
remarks: Cadastral breakdown item under Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville).

name: Total arpents
remarks: Total of the cadastral breakdown for Reserve No. 12 (Pierreville), in arpents.

name: Caughnawaga
location: On the south bank of the St. Lawrence river, in the county of Laprairie.
remarks: Part of a grant made in 1680 to the Jesuits for the conversion, instruction and subsistence of the Iroquois. The title was vested in the Iroquois under the supervision of the Indian Department, April 15, 1762, by judgement of Military Council assembled at Montreal.

name: St. Regis.
location: On the south bank of the St. Lawrence river, in the township of Dundee, county of Huntingdon. The reserve consists of the following lands:
remarks: This reserve is a part of the hunting grounds of Iroquois which were in their possession at the time of the French rule in this country.

name: St. Regis village and reserve
remarks: Breakdown item under Reserve No. 15 (St. Regis).

name: Lots in Dundee, purchased in 1892
remarks: Breakdown item under Reserve No. 15 (St. Regis).

name: Lots in Dundee, purchased in 1897
remarks: Breakdown item under Reserve No. 15 (St. Regis).

name: Cadastral list of islands
remarks: Breakdown item under Reserve No. 15 (St. Regis).

name: Islands in the St. Lawrence reported on by agent John Davidson, not included in the cadastral list
remarks: Breakdown item under Reserve No. 15 (St. Regis).
Unlabelled total line following the St. Regis (Reserve No. 15) breakdown; matches the reserve's main acreage figure.

name: Doncaster.
location: The southerly portion of the township of Doncaster, in the county of Montcalm.
tribe_band: Iroquois of Sault St. Louis, and Iroquois of Lake of Two Mountains.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Maniwaki.
location: At the confluence of the Desert river with the Gatineau river, in the county of Ottawa.
tribe_band: Algonquins of the Lake of Two Mountains.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Temiscaming.
location: At the head of Lake Temiscaming in the county of Pontiac.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Whitworth.
location: Lots 27, 28 and 29, concession 12, township of Whitworth, county of Temiscouata.
tribe_band: Amalecites of Isle Verte and Viger.
remarks: Purchased by the Department of Indian Affairs, March 31, 1877.

name: Cacouna.
location: Lot No. 66, shown on the cadastral plan of the village of Cacouna, county of Temiscouata.
tribe_band: Amalecites of Isle Verte and Viger.
remarks: Purchased by the Department of Indian Affairs, July 8, 1891.

name: Weymontaching
location: On the north side of the St. Maurice river, opposite the mouth of the Manouan river, county of Champlain.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Coucoucache
location: On the north side of the St. Maurice river, opposite the mouth of the outlet from Lake Coucoucache, county of Champlain.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (see No. 1.)

name: Escoumains
location: Near the mouth of the Escoumains river, township of Escoumains, county of Saguenay.
remarks: Purchased in 1892 by the Department of Indian Affairs.

name: Maganettawan
location: On the River Maganettawan.
remarks: Reserved under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty, September 9, 1850; subsequently surveyed and confirmed by O.C., January 31, 1853.

name: Henvey Inlet
location: At Henvey inlet, on Georgian bay.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Point Grondin
location: At Point Grondin, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Whitefish River
location: At the mouth of Whitefish river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.). The reserve originally consisted of 20,120 acres. In 1867 the north part of the reserve, containing 9,520 acres, was surrendered.

name: Spanish River
location: At the mouth of Spanish river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Whitefish Lake
location: At Whitefish lake, about 1.6 miles north of Collins inlet, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve was not surveyed until 1884. The boundaries as then surveyed were amended and established by judgement of the court of January 21, 1889. (Attorney General of Ontario vs. Francis et al.)

name: Serpent River
location: The, peninsula east of the mouth of Serpent river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Mississagi River
location: At the mouth of Mississagi river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Dokis
location: On French river
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Nipissing
location: On the north shore of Lake Nipissing.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Wanapitae
location: At Lake Wanapitae
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Huron treaty. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Thessalon
location: At the southeast corner of the township of Thessalon, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robins Huron Treaty. The reserve originally consisted of the entire township, all of which, except the present reserve, has been surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians. (See note to No. 1.)

name: French River
location: At Ogawaning, on French river
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty.

name: Garden River
location: At Garden river, near Sault Ste. Marie.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve originally consisted of a tract containing about 130,000 acres, all of which, except the present reserve, has been surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Goulais Bay.
location: At Batchewaung bay, east end of Lake Superior.
remarks: The original reserve contained about 157,440 acres, was set apart under the Robinson Huron Treaty, subsequently surveyed and finally confirmed by O.C., January 31, 1852. It was surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians in 1859. The present reserve at Goulais bay is a portion of the original reserve set apart by Orders in Council in 1879 and 1885.

name: Whitefish Island
location: At Sault Ste. Marie.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. Part of the 15th reservation.

name: Parry Island
location: In Georgian bay, near its eastern shore
remarks: Under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty the reserve was located on the mainland. The island was surveyed in lieu of that location, and the survey approved by the Commissioner of Crown Lands, November 22, 1853.

name: Shawanaga
location: In the township of Shawanaga, Parry Sound district.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Naiscoutaing
location: In the townships of Wallbridge and Harrison, Parry Sound district.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

location: Lots 34 and 35, concession 7, township of Shawanaga, Parry Sound district.
tribe_band: Shawanaga band of Ojibbewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: Vested by Order in Council of the Provincial Government, dated December 31, 1877, in the Dominion Government in trust for the Shawanaga band of Indians so long as the said band continues to occupy the said lots.

name: Temogaming
location: At Lake Temogaming
tribe_band: A band of Ojibbewas of Lake Huron who had not been provided with a reserve under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty.
remarks: Surveyed in 1884. This reserve has not been confirmed by the Provincial Government of Ontario.

name: Cockburn Island
location: On Cockburn island, Lake Huron.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: The Manitoulin islands and islands on the north shore of Lake Huron were set apart, August 9, 1836, by Sir Edmund Head, as a reserve for the Ottawas and Chippewas and any other Indians who should be allowed to settle thereon. The Manitoulin and adjacent islands were surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians October 6, 1862, and under the provisions of this surrender the present reserves, numbered 19 to 26 inclusive, were set apart.

name: Sheshegwaning
location: In the tp. of Robinson, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Obidgewong
location: In the tps. of Mills and Burpee, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: West Bay
location: In the tp. of Billings, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sucker Creek
location: In the tp. of Howland, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sheguiandah
location: In the tp. of Sheguiandah, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sucker Lake
location: In the tp. of Assiginack, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Manitoulin Island (unceded portion.)
location: The eastern peninsula of Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Cape Croker
location: Saugeen peninsula
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: The Saugeen peninsula was set apart as an Indian reserve August 9, 1836, by Sir Edmund Head, and surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians, October 13, 1854. Reserves Nos. 27, 28 and 29 were set apart under the provisions of the said surrender of October 13, 1854.

name: Chief's Point
location: Saugeen peninsula.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Saugeen reserve
location: At the southwestern corner of the Saugeen peninsula.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Hunting Reserve
location: In the township of St. Edmund.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Saugeen and Cape Croker.
remarks: Set apart from unsold Indian lands by Order in Council of November 19, 1896, as hunting grounds for the Chippewa bands of Saugeen and Cape Croker. (File 160,542.)

name: Christian Islands, viz.: - Christian, Hope and Beckwith.
location: In Lake Huron.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lakes Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron.
remarks: These islands were reserved in the surrender made by these Indians, June 5, 1856, of the islands situated in Lake Huron which they claimed. The islands in Lake Huron claimed by these Indians were ceded in error in 1850 by the Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake, Huron.

name: Gibson or Watha
location: The eastern portion of the township of Gibson, Muskoka district.
remarks: Purchased from the Provincial Government in 1881 for such members of the Oka band of Indians as might desire to settle there.

name: Rama
location: In the township of Rama, county of Ontario.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lakes Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron.
remarks: Purchased from private parties at different dates between 1843 and 1848.

name: Georgina Island
location: Georgina, Snake and Fox islands in Lake Simcoe and other islands in Lake Couchiching.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lakes Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron.
remarks: These islands have remained in the possession of the Indians, and have never been ceded by them by treaty or Purchase.

name: Scugog
location: On the island in Lake Scugog.
remarks: Purchased by these Indians with the proceeds of their own annuities, November 3, 1843.

name: Mud Lake
location: On Mud lake, in the township of Smith, county of Peterborough.
remarks: Granted in 1837 to the New England Company. Transferred to the Dominion Government in trust for the Indians by deed dated June 4, 1898, reserving 115.64 ac. The whole 664 acres (including the said 115.64 ac.) were transferred to the Dominion Government by deed dated May 12, 1900.

name: Rice Lake
location: On the north shore of Rice lake, in the county of Peterborough.
remarks: 1,120 acres of this reserve was granted in 1834 to trustees for the benefit of Indian tribes in the province. The remainder of the reserve was purchased by the Indians with their own funds.

name: Islands in the Trent waters.
location: In the counties of Peterborough and Victoria.
tribe_band: Mississaguas of Rice, Mud and Scugog Lakes.
remarks: Claimed by these Indians not to have been included in treaty of 1818, and claim subsequently admitted by the Crown Lands Department.

name: Alnwick
location: In the township of Alnwick, county of Northumberland.
remarks: Purchased from private owners at different dates between 1836 and 1870.

name: Sugar Island
location: In Rice lake, in front of the 4th and 5th concessions of Otonabee.
remarks: Purchased for the Alnwick Indians by deed from Wm. Kempt, dated January 13, 1899, for $775, from their funds.

name: Tyendinaga
location: On the bay of Quinte - the southern part of the township of Tyendinaga.
tribe_band: Mohawks of the bay of Quinte.
remarks: The reserve consisted originally of 92,700 acres granted under letters patent from the Crown in 1793, all of which, except the present reserve, has been surrendered and sold and the proceeds applied for the benefit of the Indians. Salmon island and marshes were added by Order in Council, November 13, 1900. (File 78,70.)

name: Golden Lake
location: At the southern end of Golden lake, in the county of Peterborough.
remarks: Purchased by the, Dominion Government from the Government of Ontario in 1870 as a reserve for these Indians.

name: Tuscarora
location: The township of Tuscarora and parts of the townships of Oneida and Onondaga.
tribe_band: The Six Nations, consisting of the Mohawks, Oneidas, Onodagas, Tuscaroras, Cayugas, Senecas and Delawares.
remarks: A tract six miles wide on each side of the Grand river, was granted to the Six Nations in 1784 by Sir F. Haldimand, containing about 694,910 acres. This grant was confirmed to them by letters patent in 1793 by Governor Simcoe. All of the tract, except the present reserve, has been surrendered in portions from time to time and sold for the benefit of the Indians. In 1847 the Six Nations invited the Mississaguas of the Credit to settle on their reserve, and offered them a free grant of 6,000 acres for the purpose. A number accepted, who now reside in the southwest corner of the reserve.

name: Oneida
location: In the township of Delaware, county of Middlesex.
remarks: Purchased for these Indians by the Government in 1840 with their own money which they brought with them from the United States.

name: Caradoc
location: In the township of Caradoc, county of Middlesex.
tribe_band: Chippewas of the Thames and Munsees.
remarks: Reserved by the Chippewas in the cession made by them of the 'Longwood Tract' in 1819. A small portion of the reservation was surrendered in 1834 and sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Stony Point or Aux Sables.
location: In the township of Bosanquet, county of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western districts made by them in 1827.

name: Kettle Point.
location: In the township of Bosanquet, county of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western districts made by them in 1827.
